## Goal
`docs/i18n/GLOSSARY_ES.md` (usted register, one term per concept) has no entries for the words 0.4 adds. Add draft rows, clearly marked for native-speaker review, for: setup file for someone else (helper), passphrase, practice mode, reappeared / came back, "what we did for you" (printable summary), read aloud, large text, check by hand, coverage (of sites checked), exposure score, monthly update, notification, escalation / follow-up, complaint (to a state office), removal request versus deletion request. Each row has the English concept, the Spanish term, and a register or usage note, in the table's existing format. Terms the team is not sure about get the note "needs native review" instead of a guess.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. Every new row follows the existing table columns and sits in the right section; no existing row is changed (additions only, so WO-214/219/225 edits merge cleanly).
2. All instructions use *usted*; no *tú* forms in any new note.
3. Avoids promising words: the Spanish for "erase", "guarantee", "100%", "safe" does not appear in any new row except in a note saying to avoid it (the glossary already has this convention; follow it).
4. The terms stay consistent with existing rows (e.g. "solicitud de eliminación", "sitio web de búsqueda de personas"); where a new term could clash, the row says which existing row it follows.
5. Every row for a word the app shows quotes the English label with file:line (for the 0.3 labels that exist on main; 0.4 labels that do not exist yet say "label not built yet").
6. The glossary consistency test (WO-251) passes if it exists by then; otherwise the file still parses as a Markdown table with equal column counts per row (checked by eye and by a one-line script in VENDOR_STATUS.md).

Docs/tests-only work in Codex's lane. Fake people only (Jane Q Testperson, Springfield IL), offline, Windows-safe paths. Check `tests/codex/`, `tests/grok/` and in-house `tests/test_*.py` first; don't duplicate a guard. Every claim cites file:line from main at the time of writing; re-check them.
